problems.title: Which restricted functions have inverses?
problems.question: On (−1,1), which of x²,x³,3^x,sinx,cosx have inverse functions?
problems.idea: Use the governing logarithmic identity or spatial formula, checking all domains.
formulas: A function has an inverse on its image exactly when it is one-to-one.
steps: x³,3^x and sinx are strictly increasing on this interval. x² and cosx take equal values at opposite inputs and fail injectivity.
Thus three functions have inverses.

problems.title: A positive exponential exceeds a bounded root
problems.question: How many positive roots has 3^x=(sinx)^(1/3)?
problems.idea: Use the governing logarithmic identity or spatial formula, checking all domains.
formulas: For x>0,3^x>1; the real cube root of sinx is at most 1.
steps: The two sides cannot agree for any positive input.

problems.title: A logarithm at a quadratic minimum
problems.question: Find the minimum of log₈(x²−6x+10)+2.
problems.idea: Use the governing logarithmic identity or spatial formula, checking all domains.
formulas: $x^2-6x+10=(x-3)^2+1\ge1$; base-8 logarithm increases.
steps: At x=3 the logarithm is log₈1=0. The minimum is therefore 2.

problems.title: Angle between two cube planes
problems.question: In cube ABCDA₁B₁C₁D₁, find the angle between planes BCA₁ and B₁C₁D.
problems.idea: Use the governing logarithmic identity or spatial formula, checking all domains.
formulas: Plane angle is determined by their normal vectors.
steps: Use A=(0,0,0),B=(1,0,0),C=(1,1,0),D=(0,1,0), with upper vertices at z=1.
Normals to the two planes are (1,0,1) and (−1,0,1). Their dot product is zero, giving a 90° plane angle.

problems.title: Smaller diagonal section of a hexagonal pyramid
problems.question: A regular hexagonal pyramid has height √32 and base side 8. Find its smaller diagonal-section area.
problems.idea: Use the governing logarithmic identity or spatial formula, checking all domains.
formulas: The shorter base diagonal is 8√3 and is distance 4 from the base centre.
steps: The section altitude from the apex to that chord is √(32+4²)=4√3.

problems.title: Cancel positive exponential factors
problems.question: Solve 3^(cosx)5^(sinx)=15^(cosx).
problems.idea: Use the governing logarithmic identity or spatial formula, checking all domains.
steps: Cancel the nonzero factor 3^(cosx). Equal powers of base 5 give sinx=cosx. Thus x=π/4+kπ.

problems.title: Quadrants of an even exponential graph
problems.question: In which coordinate quadrants lies f(x)=5^(−|x|)−5?
problems.idea: Use the governing logarithmic identity or spatial formula, checking all domains.
steps: All y values are negative. Negative x gives quadrant III and positive x quadrant IV; x=0 lies on the y-axis.

problems.title: Order quantities using logarithm identities
problems.question: Order a=25^[1/log₆5],b=2^[log_(√2)(2√5)],c=3^[log₉121],d=(1/2)^[log_(1/3)81].
problems.idea: Use the governing logarithmic identity or spatial formula, checking all domains.
formulas: $1/\log_b c=\log_c b$ and $b^{\log_bu}=u$.
steps: c=√121=11 and d=(1/2)^(−4)=16. Therefore c<d<b<a.

problems.title: Volume from pyramid height and face inclination
problems.question: A regular triangular pyramid has height 2√3 and face-base dihedral angle 60°. Find volume.
problems.idea: Use the governing logarithmic identity or spatial formula, checking all domains.
formulas: Base apothem $r=H/\tan60°$; equilateral base side $=2\sqrt3r$.
steps: r=2, so side=4√3 and base area=12√3. Volume=(1/3)×12√3×2√3=24.

problems.title: Three perpendicular lateral directions
problems.question: A regular triangular pyramid has planar apex angles 90°. Find lateral-area/base-area.
problems.idea: Use the governing logarithmic identity or spatial formula, checking all domains.
formulas: If each lateral edge is L, each lateral face is right isosceles, and the base side is L√2.
steps: Lateral area=3L²/2. Base area=(√3/4)(L√2)²=√3L²/2. Their ratio is √3.

problems.title: Two bounds force one input
problems.question: Count roots of 2^(x²−4x+5)=1+sin²(πx/4).
problems.idea: Use the governing logarithmic identity or spatial formula, checking all domains.
formulas: Exponent $=(x-2)^2+1\ge1$, so left side≥2; right side≤2.
steps: Equality requires both sides to be 2. The left condition forces x=2; at that input sin²(π/2)=1, so the right condition also holds.

problems.title: Ratio of shifted exponential values
problems.question: If f(x)=8^(x+1), find f(x+2)/f(x−7).
problems.idea: Use the governing logarithmic identity or spatial formula, checking all domains.
formulas: For a common base, divide powers by subtracting exponents.
steps: The ratio is 8^[(x+3)−(x−6)]=8⁹=2²⁷.

problems.title: A telescoping chain of logarithms
problems.question: Evaluate 6log₃2 log₄3 log₅4 log₆5 log₇6 log₈7.
problems.idea: Use the governing logarithmic identity or spatial formula, checking all domains.
formulas: Change every logarithm to natural logs and cancel neighbouring factors.
steps: The product of logarithms is ln2/ln8=1/3. Multiplying by 6 gives 2.

problems.title: Lateral area from height and apothem
problems.question: A regular triangular pyramid has height 4 and slant height 8. Find lateral area.
problems.idea: Use the governing logarithmic identity or spatial formula, checking all domains.
formulas: Base inradius $r=\sqrt{l^2-H^2}$; equilateral side $=2\sqrt3r$; lateral area $=Pl/2$.
steps: r=√48=4√3, so base side=24 and perimeter=72. Lateral area=72×8/2=288.

problems.title: Equal face angles give an area ratio
problems.question: A pyramid has rhombus base side 6,acute angle 30°. All face-base dihedral angles equal θ; lateral area=36. Find θ.
problems.idea: Use the governing logarithmic identity or spatial formula, checking all domains.
formulas: Base area $=6^2\sin30°=18$; projected lateral faces partition the base and scale by cosθ.
steps: Thus 36cosθ=18, so cosθ=1/2 and θ=60°.

problems.title: Absolute exponents and a zero logarithm
problems.question: Find the root sum of 199^(|x+6|)−199^(|x²+4x−12|)=log₁₉₉(cot225°).
problems.idea: Use the governing logarithmic identity or spatial formula, checking all domains.
formulas: cot225°=1, so the logarithm is zero; $x^2+4x-12=(x+6)(x-2)$.
steps: Equal powers give |x+6|=|x+6||x−2|. Either x=−6 or |x−2|=1, giving x=1,3.
The three roots sum to −6+1+3=−2.

problems.title: Express a logarithm in two supplied logs
problems.question: If log₅3=a and log₅2=b, find log₁₀45.
problems.idea: Use the governing logarithmic identity or spatial formula, checking all domains.
steps: log₅45=log₅(3²5)=2a+1, while log₅10=b+1. The ratio is (2a+1)/(b+1).

problems.title: Reciprocal logarithms reduce a long equation
problems.question: Solve (log₂(3^x−1))²+(log_(3^x−1)2)²−log₂[(3^x−1)²]−log_(3^x−1)4+2=0.
problems.idea: Use the governing logarithmic identity or spatial formula, checking all domains.
formulas: Put u=3^x−1>0,u≠1 and t=log₂u≠0. Then the expression is $t^2+t^{-2}-2t-2/t+2$.
steps: Put s=t+1/t. The equation becomes s²−2s=0, so s=0 or 2. For real nonzero t, s≤−2 or s≥2; only s=2 is possible.
t+1/t=2 gives t=1. Thus u=2,3^x=3 and x=1, which satisfies the original logarithm domains.

problems.title: A perpendicular triangular face
problems.question: A pyramid has equilateral base ABC of side 2. Face ACD is perpendicular to the base, with AD=CD=√6. Find BD.
problems.idea: Use the governing logarithmic identity or spatial formula, checking all domains.
formulas: The altitude in isosceles ACD meets AC at its midpoint O and is perpendicular to the base.
steps: DO²=6−1=5. In the equilateral base BO=√3. Thus BD=√(DO²+BO²)=√8.

problems.title: Octahedron formed by cube face centres
problems.question: A regular square prism has square lateral faces and lateral area 144. Find volume of the polyhedron of all face-incircle centres.
problems.idea: Use the governing logarithmic identity or spatial formula, checking all domains.
formulas: The prism is a cube; its six face centres form a regular octahedron with volume one sixth of the cube.
steps: 4s²=144 gives s=6. The octahedron consists of two square pyramids: square diagonal 6,base area 18,and heights 3.

problems.title: An exponential inside a logarithm
problems.question: Which listed positive x satisfies log₃(x^(x⁴))=log_(1/3)(0.25)?
problems.idea: Use the governing logarithmic identity or spatial formula, checking all domains.
steps: For x=√2, x⁴=4 and x^(x⁴)=(√2)⁴=4. It works.
For 0<x≤1 the power is at most 1. For x>1, x⁴lnx is strictly increasing, so there is no second positive solution.

problems.title: An exponential system with a logarithmic difference
problems.question: Solve 3^x2^y=576 and log_(√2)(y−x)=4. Find x+y.
problems.idea: Use the governing logarithmic identity or spatial formula, checking all domains.
formulas: The logarithm gives y−x=(√2)⁴=4.
steps: Substitute y=x+4: 16·6^x=576, so 6^x=36 and x=2. Then y=6 and x+y=8.

problems.title: Reciprocal logarithm in an exponent
problems.question: Which listed x satisfies 2^[log_x2]=x^[1/log_(4x)x]?
problems.idea: Use the governing logarithmic identity or spatial formula, checking all domains.
formulas: Domain x>0,x≠1,x≠1/4. Reciprocal-log identity makes the right side 4x.
steps: Put t=log₂x≠0. The equation is 2^(1/t)=2^(t+2), so t²+2t−1=0.
t=−1±√2 gives x=2^(−1±√2), both admissible. Only 2^(√2−1) is listed.
problems.answer: $2^{\sqrt2-1}$ among the choices; both roots are $2^{-1\pm\sqrt2}$.

problems.title: Tetrahedron volume from edge angles
problems.question: Three lateral edges have length a and pairwise angles 45°,45°,60°. Find volume.
problems.idea: Use the governing logarithmic identity or spatial formula, checking all domains.
formulas: $V=a^3\sqrt{\det G}/6$, where G is their unit-vector Gram matrix.
steps: detG=1+2cos45°cos45°cos60°−cos²45°−cos²45°−cos²60°=1/4.

problems.title: An alternating-vertex tetrahedron in a parallelepiped
problems.question: A right parallelepiped ABCDA₁B₁C₁D₁ has volume 6. Find tetrahedron AD₁CB₁ volume.
problems.idea: Use the governing logarithmic identity or spatial formula, checking all domains.
formulas: An affine map preserves volume ratios; use a unit cube model.
steps: From A, the three edge vectors to D₁,C,B₁ have coordinate columns (0,1,1),(1,1,0),(1,0,1). Their determinant magnitude is 2.
The tetrahedron occupies 2/6=1/3 of the parallelepiped. Volume=6/3=2.
